{{Short description|Type of ringed space}}
{{Technical|date=November 2023}}
In [[algebraic geometry]], a '''sheaf of algebras''' on a [[ringed space]] ''X'' is a [[sheaf of commutative rings]] on ''X'' that is also a [[sheaf of modules|sheaf of <math>\mathcal{O}_X</math>-modules]]. It is [[quasi-coherent sheaf|quasi-coherent]] if it is so as a module.

When ''X'' is a [[scheme (mathematics)|scheme]], just like a ring, one can take the [[global Spec]] of a quasi-coherent sheaf of algebras: this results in the contravariant [[functor]] <math>\operatorname{Spec}_X</math> from the [[category (mathematics)|category]] of quasi-coherent (sheaves of) <math>\mathcal{O}_X</math>-algebras on ''X'' to the category of schemes that are '''affine''' over ''X'' (defined below). Moreover, it is an [[equivalence of categories|equivalence]]: the quasi-inverse is given by sending an affine morphism <math>f: Y \to X</math> to <math>f_* \mathcal{O}_Y.</math><ref>{{harvnb|EGA|1971|loc=Ch. I, Théorème 9.1.4.}}</ref>

== Affine morphism ==
A [[morphism of schemes]] <math>f: X \to Y</math> is called '''affine''' if <math>Y</math> has an open affine cover <math>U_i</math>'s such that <math>f^{-1}(U_i)</math> are affine.<ref>{{harvnb|EGA|1971|loc=Ch. I, Definition 9.1.1.}}</ref> For example, a [[finite morphism]] is affine. An affine morphism is [[quasi-compact morphism|quasi-compact]] and [[separated morphism|separated]]; in particular, the [[direct image functor|direct image]] of a quasi-coherent sheaf along an affine morphism is quasi-coherent.

The [[Base change (scheme theory)|base change]] of an affine morphism is affine.<ref>{{Citation | title=Stacks Project, Tag 01S5 | url=https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01S5}}.</ref> 

Let <math>f: X \to Y</math> be an affine morphism between schemes and <math>E</math> a [[locally ringed space]] together with a map <math>g: E \to Y</math>. Then the natural map between the sets:
:<math>\operatorname{Mor}_Y(E, X) \to \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal{O}_Y\text{-alg}}(f_* \mathcal{O}_X, g_* \mathcal{O}_E)</math>
is bijective.<ref>{{harvnb|EGA|1971|loc=Ch. I, Proposition 9.1.5.}}</ref>

== Examples ==
*Let <math>f: \widetilde{X} \to X</math> be the [[Normalization of an algebraic variety|normalization]] of an algebraic variety ''X''. Then, since ''f'' is finite, <math>f_* \mathcal{O}_{\widetilde{X}}</math> is quasi-coherent and <math>\operatorname{Spec}_X(f_* \mathcal{O}_{\widetilde{X}}) = \widetilde{X}</math>.
*Let <math>E</math> be a locally free sheaf of finite rank on a scheme ''X''. Then <math>\operatorname{Sym}(E^*)</math> is a quasi-coherent <math>\mathcal{O}_X</math>-algebra and <math>\operatorname{Spec}_X(\operatorname{Sym}(E^*)) \to X</math> is the associated vector bundle over ''X'' (called the total space of <math>E</math>.)
*More generally, if ''F'' is a coherent sheaf on ''X'', then one still has <math>\operatorname{Spec}_X(\operatorname{Sym}(F)) \to X</math>, usually called the abelian hull of ''F''; see [[Cone (algebraic geometry)#Examples]].

== The formation of direct images ==
Given a ringed space ''S'', there is the category <math>C_S</math> of pairs <math>(f, M)</math> consisting of a ringed space morphism <math>f: X \to S</math> and an <math>\mathcal{O}_X</math>-module <math>M</math>. Then the formation of direct images determines the contravariant functor from <math>C_S</math> to the category of pairs consisting of an <math>\mathcal{O}_S</math>-algebra ''A'' and an ''A''-module ''M'' that sends each pair <math>(f, M)</math> to the pair <math>(f_* \mathcal{O}, f_* M)</math>.

Now assume ''S'' is a scheme and then let <math>\operatorname{Aff}_S \subset C_S</math> be the subcategory consisting of pairs <math>(f: X \to S, M)</math> such that <math>f</math> is an affine morphism between schemes and <math>M</math> a quasi-coherent sheaf on <math>X</math>. Then the above functor determines the equivalence between <math>\operatorname{Aff}_S</math> and the category of pairs <math>(A, M)</math> consisting of an <math>\mathcal{O}_S</math>-algebra ''A'' and a quasi-coherent <math>A</math>-module <math>M</math>.<ref>{{harvnb|EGA|1971|loc=Ch. I, Théorème 9.2.1.}}</ref>

The above equivalence can be used (among other things) to do the following construction. As before, given a scheme ''S'', let ''A'' be a quasi-coherent <math>\mathcal{O}_S</math>-algebra and then take its global Spec: <math>f: X = \operatorname{Spec}_S(A) \to S</math>. Then, for each quasi-coherent ''A''-module ''M'', there is a corresponding quasi-coherent <math>\mathcal{O}_X</math>-module <math>\widetilde{M}</math> such that <math>f_* \widetilde{M} \simeq M,</math> called the sheaf associated to ''M''. Put in another way, <math>f_*</math> determines an equivalence between the category of quasi-coherent <math>\mathcal{O}_X</math>-modules and the quasi-coherent <math>A</math>-modules.
